Tell the resident to leave the affected area, avoid operating switches or equipment if a gas leak is suspected, and contact emergency services from a safe location. Do not ask the resident to investigate the source, relight equipment, or perform repairs. Notify the on-call property contact after the resident is safe, where appropriate.

### Electrical danger

For sparks, exposed conductors, shocks, burning odors, or water contacting electrical equipment, tell the resident to keep away from the affected area and not touch exposed wiring or wet electrical equipment. If there is immediate danger, move to safety and contact emergency services. Dispatch only qualified personnel through the authorized process.

For nonemergency work, staff should follow the property's verified notice and access procedure, document the appointment window, and identify the authorized worker. Emergency entry rules must come from the actual lease and applicable law; this synthetic policy does not establish a legal right of entry or a notice period.

If access cannot be confirmed, the system should record the failed coordination attempt and request human follow-up. It must not mark a job complete solely because a visit was scheduled.

Route reports of persistent dampness, recurring condensation, or visible suspected mold for human inspection. The AI must not identify a species, determine toxicity, diagnose a medical condition, or certify that an area is safe based on a photo or text description alone.

If an occupant reports severe symptoms or an immediate health emergency, advise seeking appropriate medical or emergency assistance; do not diagnose the cause.

## 4. Pest reports

Record the pest described and where/when it was observed. Route to the approved pest-control workflow. Do not recommend restricted pesticides or improvised chemical mixtures. The system must not assert that a particular resident caused an infestation without verified evidence and an authorized review process.
